findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block / no ACL restriction
findings.description: The bucket has no ACL specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricting public access, leaving it potentially exposed to public read/write depending on account-level defaults.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket storing ledger export data, meaning sensitive financial data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational runbook data (which may contain sensitive operational details) is stored unencrypted.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be permanently deleted without recovery, increasing risk of accidental or malicious data loss for archived reports.
force_destroy = true permits irreversible deletion of all objects in a bucket holding financial ledger exports.

The object is uploaded to a bucket lacking server-side encryption configuration and does not specify its own server_side_encryption/kms_key_id, so this potentially sensitive vendor roster file is stored in cleartext.
